prompt.title: Optional discussion prompts
prompt.instructions: Your teacher may ask you to think about one of these. Nothing here is required, and nothing is collected.
prompt.engage: What evidence would distinguish an infectious disease from a dietary deficiency?
prompt.explore1: Which observations are from real investigations, and which come from our simulation?
prompt.explain1: Why might a cell with plenty of sugar still lack sufficient ATP?
prompt.explore2: Which variables must be held constant to compare decomposition fairly?
prompt.explain2: What changed in the food, and what happened inside a cell?
prompt.elaborate: How can corn-heavy diets have different nutritional outcomes?
prompt.evaluate: Which changes to food availability could support nutritional adequacy?

kernel.removed: Removed at the mill: germ and bran
kernel.caption.whole_untreated: Whole kernel: every part is kept, but much of the niacin is bound.
kernel.caption.whole_nixtamalized: Nixtamalized: bound niacin is freed. None is created.
kernel.caption.degermed_unfortified: Degermed: the germ and the bran are removed, and niacin goes with them.
kernel.caption.degermed_fortified: Fortified: niacin is added after degerming.
kernel.caption.diverse: Diverse foods: several sources of niacin and tryptophan.
kernel.explain.whole_untreated: Untreated whole corn keeps its germ and bran, so the niacin is still in the food. But most of it is bound to other molecules and passes through the body without being absorbed. A diet of mostly untreated corn can still run short of usable niacin.
kernel.explain.whole_nixtamalized: Nixtamalization was developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas. The corn is cooked and soaked in limewater, an alkaline solution. This frees the bound niacin so the body can absorb it. The amount of niacin in the corn does not go up; the usable share does.
kernel.explain.degermed_unfortified: Industrial milling removes the germ and the bran. That takes away oil that turns rancid in storage, so the meal keeps longer. It also takes away much of the niacin and protein. What is left is mostly starch: plenty of calories, little usable niacin.
kernel.explain.degermed_fortified: Fortified cornmeal is degermed first. Then niacin is added back at the mill. Usable niacin goes up. Calories stay the same.
kernel.explain.diverse: A varied diet does not depend on one food. Beans, greens, eggs, milk, meat and fish add niacin and the amino acid tryptophan, which the body can turn into a little niacin.

hist.title: Historical evidence: Goldberger's investigations
hist.intro: These pages show records from Dr. Joseph Goldberger's pellagra investigations, as summarized in your lesson materials. Use your handouts as the main source.
hist.not_model: These numbers are historical records. The simulation did not produce them and cannot change them. The simulation's own results are illustrations and will not match these counts.
hist.ethics: Some of these studies were done on people in orphanages, a hospital and a prison, in ways that would not be allowed today. They are shown here as documents to examine, not as experiments to repeat.
hist.categories: One record uses the racial categories written in the original report. They show how the report grouped people, not a difference in how bodies use niacin.

hist.prison.note: This investigation deliberately made people ill. A study like this would not be approved today.

help.title: How to use this sandbox
help.what: This is a sandbox, not a game. There is nothing to win and nothing is graded. Change something, watch what happens, and use what you see in your class discussion.
help.start: Press Start to run the clock. Pause stops everything. Step moves time forward a little while paused. Reset returns the body and the community to the well-nourished starting point; your settings stay as they are.
help.diet: Diet and workload: choose a food and how it was processed. The usable niacin changes with them. Calories change the fuel supply. Workload changes how much ATP the cell must use.
help.time: A lack of niacin takes time to show. The person starts well nourished. With a time lapse on, days pass and the NAD pool slowly follows the diet. Recovery takes time too.
help.views: The cell view shows NAD⁺ picking up electrons to become NADH, handing them on, and being used again. The population view shows the same diet across many modeled people.
help.food: Food and decomposition opens a corn kernel cross-section and a storage test with its own clock.
help.compare: Graph and comparison: keep a run as a baseline, change one thing, press Reset and run again. The kept run stays as a dashed line. You can download the numbers as a file; nothing is sent anywhere.
help.model: Everything here is a simplified model. Its numbers are relative, not real measurements, and pellagra involves more than ATP alone. The historical evidence pages show real records, kept separate from the model.
help.keyboard: Keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls. Enter or Space presses a button. Arrow keys move a slider or scroll a focused panel. Space starts or pauses, N or the Right arrow steps, and R resets, when no control is using that key. Escape closes an open panel. With no panel open, Escape, or Tab past the last control, leaves the simulation.
help.limits: If this tab is hidden or covered, the browser pauses the simulation until you come back. Screen readers get short spoken summaries, not a full description of the picture.
key.nad: NAD⁺: an empty carrier, ready to accept electrons
key.nadh: NADH: the same carrier, now carrying electrons
key.adp: ADP: used ATP, ready to be recharged
key.pyruvate: Pyruvate: what glycolysis makes from glucose
key.oxygen: O₂: oxygen, the final electron acceptor
key.proton: H⁺: protons pumped across the inner membrane
key.niacin: Niacin (vitamin B3): needed to keep the NAD pool stocked
